symptom: A project made by `mxcli new --version 11.14` fails its very first build with `error: release version 25 not supported`, and installing a JDK 25 moves the failure to boot (`UnsupportedClassVersionError … class file version 69.0`)
cause: Mendix 11.14's `mx create-project` writes `JavaVersion = 25`, but mxcli builds and launches the runtime on **JDK 21** and validates it (`resolveJDK21` refuses any other `JAVA_HOME`). Compiling for 25 and running on 21 cannot work in either direction — and 11.14's own runtime bundles are still Java 21 class files (major version 65)
file: `cmd/mxcli/cmd_new_java.go` (`alignJavaVersion`, `runtimeMaxJavaVersion`), called from `cmd_new.go` **before** the first build; the launcher side is `cmd/mxcli/docker/detect.go` (`resolveJDK21`)
insight: **Lower the project, do not raise the JDK.** Set `JavaVersion` to what the runtime launcher actually uses, and only when the project asks for MORE — so it is a no-op on 11.13 and disappears by itself when the launcher becomes version-aware. Order matters: align BEFORE `SettleGeneratedSources`, or that build is the thing that fails. Mendix then warns "Java versions below 25 are deprecated", which is a deprecation on a project that builds rather than an error on one that does not. An unparseable version is left alone rather than overwritten. `runtimeMaxJavaVersion` and `resolveJDK21` must move together — there is a test asserting it. ako/mxcli-maintenance #1, #3
